properties.name: Every write and every approval records both the agent that made it and the person it acted for, so a decision an agent makes under a person's delegation is attributed truthfully
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-09-29, in the dev_reflow2 hub session, relayed by the hub agent: "Fix all the root causes and go with the 7 ideas you'd promote". This is idea 1, dec:idea-an-agent-acting-for-a-person-is-recorded-as-both, from the triage of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29.
properties.statement:
Every write, and every approval, records both the AGENT that made it and the PRINCIPAL it acted for. The ACTS_FOR rung, designed on 2026-07-22 and deferred, is built. The principal stays the approver of record, because the authority is theirs. The agent is recorded beside the principal as the party that acted. A standing delegation is part of the record, so a reader can tell "the owner decided" from "an agent decided under the owner's delegation".

Counter-argument kept from the brainstorm: an agent's identity is self-declared. So it serves ATTRIBUTION, never AUTHORITY, and must never widen what an approval may settle.

Found by the two-agent exercise (I1, I21): a separate owner agent's verdicts could only be recorded as the signed-in person's, and the owner agent itself called that a failure of test 2 (who asserts).
